**Finding: missing** (Section 10 — Effect of Expiry or Termination)

The agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return obligation:

- **§10.1** only ends our access "after any agreed transition period" — it presumes a transition period without creating any entitlement to one or any pricing basis.
- **§10.2** covers Deliverable delivery and refunds, not Customer Data.
- **§16.5** addresses only Confidential Information and defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" — Section 11 does not exist in the document, and Section 15 contains only processing-purpose and privacy-compliance duties, with no return, export or deletion mechanic.
- No occurrences of "export" (in the data sense) or "delet" anywhere in the document.

Because neither the preferred nor the fallback position (90 days' assistance + 30-day export) is met anywhere, this fails the fallback on a material term. Redline validated (`ok:true`) inserting a new **§10.3** at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter — with routine-backup and legal-retention carve-outs mirroring the existing §16.5 language so the clause fits the document's own bargain.
